module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 508

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/508](https://www.erdosproblems.com/508)

proven by considering the [Moser-Spindel graph]
or the [Golomb graph]
*At least 4 colors are required:* [Moser-Spindel graph](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moser-Spindel)
*At least 4 colors are required:* [Golomb graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golomb_graph)
*At least 5 colors are required:* [de Grey 2018](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.02385)
-/

@[expose] public section

open SimpleGraph
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace Erdos508

scoped notation "χ(ℝ²)" => SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber (UnitDistancePlaneGraph Set.univ)

/--
The Hadwiger–Nelson problem asks: How many colors are required to color the plane
such that no two points at distance 1 from each other have the same color?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem HadwigerNelsonProblem :
    χ(ℝ²) = answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/--
Aubrey de Grey improved the lower bound for the chromatic number of the plane
to 5 in 2018 using a graph that has >1000 nodes.

"The chromatic number of the plane is at least 5" Aubrey D. N. J. de Grey, 2018
(https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1804.02385)
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem HadwigerNelsonAtLeastFive :
    5 ≤ χ(ℝ²) := by
  sorry

/--
The "chromatic number of the plane" is at least 4. This can be
proven by considering the [Moser-Spindel graph](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moser-Spindel)
or the [Golomb graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golomb_graph) graph.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem HadwigerNelsonAtLeast4 : 4 ≤ χ(ℝ²) := by
  sorry

/--
This upper bound for the chromatic number of the plane was
observed by John R. Isbell. His approach was dividing the
plane into hexagons of uniform size and coloring them with a repeating
pattern. A proof can probably be found in:

Soifer, Alexander (2008), The Mathematical Coloring Book: Mathematics of Coloring and the Colorful Life of its Creators, New York: Springer, ISBN 978-0-387-74640-1

An alternative approach that uses square tiling was highlighted by László Székely.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 52]
theorem HadwigerNelsonAtMostSeven :
    χ(ℝ²) ≤ 7 := by
  sorry

/-- The chromatic number of the plane is at least 3.

This is proven by considering an equilateral triangle in the plane. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 5]
theorem HadwigerNelsonAtLeastThree : 3 ≤ χ(ℝ²) :=
  le_chromaticNumber_of_pairwise_adj (by simp)
    ![(⟨!₂[0, 0], Set.mem_univ _⟩ : ↥(Set.univ : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)))),
      (⟨!₂[1, 0], Set.mem_univ _⟩ : ↥(Set.univ : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)))),
      (⟨!₂[0.5, Real.sqrt 3 / 2], Set.mem_univ _⟩ : ↥(Set.univ : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))))] <| by
    simp [pairwise_fin_succ_iff_of_isSymm, Fin.forall_fin_succ]
    simp [UnitDistancePlaneGraph, PiLp.dist_eq_of_L2, Real.dist_eq, div_pow, Subtype.dist_eq]
    norm_num

reformulations.difference: The source's "smallest number of colours required to colour ℝ² such that no two points of the same colour are distance 1 apart" is stated as Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber : ℕ∞` of `UnitDistancePlaneGraph Set.univ`. That graph lives on the subtype `↥(Set.univ : Set ℝ²)`, not on ℝ² itself, and the value is an infimum in ℕ∞ that could in principle be ⊤. The same encoding is used in HadwigerNelsonAtLeastFive, HadwigerNelsonAtLeast4, HadwigerNelsonAtMostSeven and HadwigerNelsonAtLeastThree.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (1) The metric on the subtype is definitionally the ambient Euclidean (L2) metric on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)`. (2) `Equiv.Set.univ ℝ²` is a graph isomorphism onto the unit-distance graph on ℝ², so by `chromaticNumber_congr` the chromatic numbers agree. (3) `Colorable n` holds iff there is a map c : ℝ² → Fin n with c x ≠ c y whenever dist x y = 1. So `chromaticNumber = ⨅ {n | Colorable n}` is exactly the Hadwiger–Nelson number: the least n admitting such a colouring. It is finite (≤ 7, Isbell), so the ⊤ value is never reached. Colourings are arbitrary functions with no measurability condition, as in the source; Lean's classical logic gives the ZFC reading. I proved (1), (2) and (3) in /workspace/review/scratch3.lean.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/508 (read through the rendering proxy https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/508; direct curl was blocked by Cloudflare)
https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.02385 (de Grey, 'The chromatic number of the plane is at least 5'; abstract: smallest graph has 1581 vertices)
review.notes:
No misformalization found. All five declarations match erdosproblems.com/508:
- the main question `χ(ℝ²) = answer(sorry)` in ℕ∞, tagged `research open`, which matches the source's OPEN;
- the bounds ≥5 (de Grey 2018, research solved), ≥4 (Moser spindle / Golomb graph, research solved) and ≤7 (hexagon tiling, textbook);
- ≥3 (equilateral triangle, textbook), which is actually proved in the file using only propext/choice/Quot.sound.

Minor, non-mathematical observations (not reported as findings):
(a) The module docstring has a stray, duplicated fragment: "proven by considering the [Moser-Spindel graph] or the [Golomb graph]".
(b) The `HadwigerNelsonAtMostSeven` docstring credits László Székely with a square-tiling 7-colouring. None of the sources I read mention this. I could not verify it, but it does not affect the statement.
(c) `HadwigerNelsonAtLeast4` is tagged `research solved`. `textbook` would also fit for a 1961 classical result, but both tags record it as settled, so this is not a status issue.
(d) The source's fractional-chromatic-number remarks (≥ 4 by Matolcsi–Ruzsa–Varga–Zsámboki; ≤ 4.359… by Croft) are not formalized. That is an omission, not a misformalization.

Status: the page was last edited 22 January 2026, still says OPEN and gives 5 ≤ χ ≤ 7. Wikipedia agrees (5, 6 or 7). So no status issues.
